title: Late Devonian (Frasnian–Famennian) extinction
summary: Two pulses of oceanic anoxia, the Lower and Upper Kellwasser events, accompanied massive marine biodiversity losses near the Frasnian–Famennian boundary. At the Steinbruch Schmidt quarry in Germany the boundary is dated to 371.870 million years ago, and the two Kellwasser horizons formed over roughly 90 and 110 thousand years.

uncertainty.note: Frasnian-Famennian boundary dated 371.870 +/-0.108 Ma (Da Silva et al.); start and end here are that error span. Percival et al. constrain the boundary to 371.93-371.78 Ma.

as_recorded.value: a high-precision age of 371.870 ± 0.108 Ma for the F–F boundary

where.modern_name: Steinbruch Schmidt quarry, near Bad Wildungen, Hesse, Germany (Kellerwald; boundary section; the event was global)
where.historical_name: Shelf sea on the southern margin of Laurussia (no human geography)

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service

importance.justification: One of the Big Five mass extinctions of the Phanerozoic.

reviewer_note: Pin is Bad Wildungen as a proxy for the Steinbruch Schmidt quarry, which Percival et al. place near there; the quarry has no coordinates on opened pages. No opened page gives a percentage of species lost, so the summary omits one. The id says 372 Ma; the sourced boundary age is 371.87 Ma.
